intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene (610819) on chromosome 3p22.1.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in mitochondrial carrier family gene SLC25A38 cause nonsyndromic autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The abstract says SLC25A38 mutations cause nonsyndromic autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia. It does not use the label SIDBA2 or say the disease is pyridoxine-refractory; these details are not in the abstract supplied.

checks.claim: The SLC25A38 gene is located on chromosome 3p22.1.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosome location, but standard nomenclature such as a gene's chromosomal location counts as supported under the rules.

paragraphs.text: Sideroblastic anemia-2 is an autosomal recessive, nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia (Guernsey et al., 2009). The morphologic hallmark of the sideroblastic anemias is ringed sideroblasts. These are bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria (Guernsey et al., 2009). Manabe et al. (1982) reported onset in infancy and no response to pyridoxine. Jardine et al. (1994) described severe, transfusion-dependent anemia.

checks.claim: Sideroblastic anemia-2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states that this form is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Sideroblastic anemia-2 is a nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states that this form is nonsyndromic and congenital.

checks.claim: The morphologic hallmark of the sideroblastic anemias is ringed sideroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Ringed sideroblasts are bone marrow erythroid precursors that contain pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria.
checks.evidence_quote: ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Manabe et al. (1982) reported that sideroblastic anemia-2 begins in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: A female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia is described.
checks.explanation: The paper describes one female infant with congenital sideroblastic anemia, so onset in infancy is consistent with it. However, the claim generalizes to the disease, and the abstract does not name or classify the condition as sideroblastic anemia-2.

checks.claim: Manabe et al. (1982) reported that sideroblastic anemia-2 does not respond to pyridoxine.
checks.evidence_quote: which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case.
checks.explanation: The paper reports pyridoxine unresponsiveness only in this one case. The draft states it as a feature of sideroblastic anemia-2 in general, which the paper does not do.

checks.claim: Jardine et al. (1994) described sideroblastic anemia-2 as a severe anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth. Their haemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not use the word 'severe'. The haemoglobin levels of 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl and the need for transfusion show that the anaemia was severe. The paper attributes the condition to an autosomal recessive trait rather than naming it 'sideroblastic anemia-2'.

checks.claim: Jardine et al. (1994) described sideroblastic anemia-2 as a transfusion-dependent anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that the anaemia was transfusion dependent.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) studied families with nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia that was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. They noted that the morphologic hallmark of the sideroblastic anemias is ringed sideroblasts in the bone marrow.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) studied families with nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The study of this disorder is supported. The abstract does not mention families; positional cloning implies them, but families are not described.

checks.claim: The nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia in the families studied by Guernsey et al. (2009) was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract supports autosomal recessive inheritance. It does not describe the families studied.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the morphologic hallmark of the sideroblastic anemias is ringed sideroblasts in the bone marrow.
checks.evidence_quote: whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria
checks.explanation: The abstract states this; it describes ringed sideroblasts as bone marrow cells.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) defined an autosomal recessive form of nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia associated with mutations in the SLC25A38 gene.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) defined an autosomal recessive form of nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia defined by Guernsey et al. (2009) is associated with mutations in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematologic disorders. Jardine et al. (1994) noted that ALAS2 mutations had been reported in patients with X-linked sideroblastic anemia. SIDBA2 is an autosomal recessive form of congenital sideroblastic anemia associated with SLC25A38 mutation (Guernsey et al., 2009).

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of hematologic disorders that include both congenital and acquired forms.
checks.evidence_quote: The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematological disorders
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Jardine et al. (1994) noted that ALAS2 mutations had been reported in patients with X-linked sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: While mutations of the erythroid-specific delta-aminolaevulinate synthase gene (ALAS2) at Xp11.21 have been reported in patients with X linked sideroblastic anaemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: SIDBA2 is an autosomal recessive form of congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract describes this form as autosomal recessive and congenital. The SIDBA2 label is the draft's name for it.

checks.claim: SIDBA2 is associated with mutation in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) used positional cloning to define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia. They found that it was associated with mutations in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) used positional cloning to define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) found that the newly defined autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia was associated with mutations in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The SLC25A38 gene encodes a mitochondrial carrier family protein.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The protein encoded by the SLC25A38 gene is erythroid-specific.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Manabe et al. (1982) reported a patient with congenital sideroblastic anemia who did not respond to pyridoxine therapy. The patients reported by Jardine et al. (1994) had transfusion-dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia from birth.

checks.claim: Manabe et al. (1982) reported a patient with congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: A female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia is described.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly describes a patient with congenital sideroblastic anemia.

checks.claim: The patient with congenital sideroblastic anemia reported by Manabe et al. (1982) did not respond to pyridoxine therapy.
checks.evidence_quote: which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that this patient did not respond to pyridoxine therapy.

checks.claim: The patients reported by Jardine et al. (1994) had transfusion-dependent sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that both patients' anaemia was transfusion dependent.

checks.claim: The sideroblastic anemia in the patients reported by Jardine et al. (1994) was refractory to pyridoxine.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the anaemia was pyridoxine-refractory.

checks.claim: The sideroblastic anemia in the patients reported by Jardine et al. (1994) was present from birth.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the anaemia was present from birth.
